closedFindings.confirmation: When all candidates are absent, a recorded DNS resolution failure takes precedence over an earlier resolved-address count. The existing failure-distinction test includes valid address -> removed -> resolutionFailed -> windowEnded and asserts zero TCP destinations.

Before NWConnection creation, checkedHost rejects name fallback and requires the exact expected IP family and raw address bytes; IPv6 link-local also requires matching SDK interface index. The existing scope test uses the actual lo0 index for its SDK-roundtrip assertion.

DNS-SD refs deactivate and deallocate on the same required serial queue before context ownership is released. C pointers do not cross async hops. Raw two-byte sockaddr header reads precede bounded full-host or short-mask decoding.

TCP requires an explicit normal windowEnded and a closed stream; cancellation, overflow, invalidation and unexpected termination cannot authorize partial discovery results. Address TTL and current interface ownership are rechecked before connecting.

reviewedBoundaries: Only _remotepairing._tcp in local. is browsed; SRV targets are restricted to local. or localhost. DNS-SD resolves addresses before any candidate TCP connection.
A TCP-only attempt has no send/receive or TLS/session/pair/account/sign/install behavior, closes on its single completion, and does not establish service identity or automatic renewal.

The interface snapshot includes IP-address nodes and raw flags, including ineligible interface addresses, but not unaddressed AF_LINK nodes or the complete route table. Narrow eligible interface classification is not proof that no VPN exists.
Reports expose bounded counts, categories, phases and normalized errors; service names, addresses, scope identifiers, interface names, dynamic ports and TXT stay out of the report.
